text:
maria (CS): Quick check-in for AstraGrid onboarding — noticed tail latency spikes during batch processing tests yesterday (p95 ~ 420ms on us-west). Thinking proactive perf play: int8 quant + tiered routing for heavy inference bursts. Thoughts?

alex (SE): +1 on int8 pilot. We should run a short accuracy regression on the 10k oracle prompts first, then canary traffic at 5% before flipping. Also propose a fallback to fp16 if quality drops.

jon (ML): Agree. For AstraGrid's typical seq len (<=512) int8 should be fine but watch for hallucination rate on named-entity extracts. I'd add a KV cache prefix for repeated customer prompts to shave latency.

sara (AstraGrid): Thanks — accuracy is critical for our compliance checks. What % quality delta would you expect with int8? Also, can we keep peak SLA at 200ms p95 for small requests?

alex (SE): Expect <1.5% token-level perplexity change for our model family on the eval set we use. For small requests, batching config + routing to lower-latency hosts should keep p95 near target — plan: route policy by request size and customer tier.

maria (CS): Proposed rollout plan: 1) run 10k eval on int8 vs fp16, 2) configure routing rule: size<256 -> low-latency pool in us-west; size>=256 -> cost-optimized pool, 3) canary at 5% for 24h, 4) check eval metrics + user QA, 5) gradual ramp. Schedule win?

jon (ML): I'll own the eval and attach diff graphs. Quick snippet to run quant eval:

```bash
python tools/eval_quant.py --model redwood-tt-1 --quant int8 --prompts data/astra_oracle.json --out reports/astra_int8.json
```

alex (SE): Routing snippet (Redwood config):

```yaml
routes:
  - name: low-latency-pool
    match: request.tokens <= 256 and customer == "AstraGrid"
    pool: us-west-ll
  - name: default-cost-optimized
    match: true
    pool: cost-optimized
```

maria (CS): Canary-bot initiating canary window once we agree. Are there any regulatory logging needs for AstraGrid while on canary?

sara (AstraGrid): Yes, we need audit logs for every inference call for 30 days. Is that easy to enable for the canary subset?

alex (SE): Yes, we can enable request-level audit logging per-route. Add `audit_log: true` to the route config for the canary.

jon (ML): I'll put expected metric thresholds in the eval report: token-perplexity delta, top-level task accuracy delta, p95 latency target. If any exceed thresholds we abort and fallback to fp16 automatically.

maria (CS): Action items: jon -> deliver eval report by EOD Thu, alex -> prepare route + audit config, sara -> confirm acceptance criteria for accuracy, maria -> schedule 5% canary Fri 09:00 PT. Ping me if blockers. :thumbsup:

canary-bot: Canary scheduled for 2026-03-27 09:00 PT at 5% traffic to pool us-west-ll.

sara (AstraGrid): Sounds good — thanks everyone. We'll loop in our compliance lead once jon shares the eval numbers.

alex (SE): One more note: enable KV prefix caching for repeated verification prompts. Minimal change but big latency win. I'll add it to the canary config.

maria (CS): Great — closing here for now. Will post follow-up with links to eval + route PRs. :white_check_mark:
